title: Pandas Data Cleaning Basics: Nulls and Duplicates
audience: Complete beginners to data cleaning who know basic Python syntax (variables, functions, lists) but have never used pandas before.
prerequisites: Basic Python (variables, functions, lists, running a .py script). No prior pandas or data engineering experience required.
outcomes: Explain why missing values and duplicate rows silently corrupt reports and metrics.
Detect missing values in a pandas DataFrame with isna() and isnull().
Fill or drop missing values deliberately with fillna() and dropna(), choosing the right strategy per column.
Detect duplicate rows with duplicated(), including partial-key duplicates.
Remove duplicate rows deterministically with drop_duplicates() while keeping a defined row.
Verify a small cleaning script with automated tests.
business_scenario: A small online newsletter platform exports its subscriber signup list from a web form to a CSV file every night. The export regularly has blank rows where the visitor skipped an optional field (like a name or referral source), and it contains duplicate rows for the same email address because the signup form silently retries when a visitor double-clicks 'Subscribe'. The marketing team cannot count real subscribers or send a clean welcome email batch until the file is cleaned.
deliverable: A clean_subscribers.py script that reads subscribers.csv, produces clean_subscribers.csv (one row per unique, non-blank-email subscriber) and a subscribers_report.txt summary, and passes the provided pytest suite.
validation_criteria: pytest against tests/test_clean_subscribers.py exits with status 0.
clean_subscribers.csv contains no rows with a missing email address.
clean_subscribers.csv contains exactly one row per unique email address (first signup kept, earliest signup_date wins on ties).
Missing optional text fields (name, referral_source) are filled with the literal string 'unknown' rather than left blank or dropped.
acquired_skills: Detecting missing values in a DataFrame with isna()/isnull().
Choosing between fillna() and dropna() per column based on business rules.
Detecting exact and key-based duplicate rows with duplicated().
Writing a small deterministic pandas cleaning script validated by automated tests.

duration_minutes.practical_breakdown_note: The 50 practical minutes are NOT all spent on the final lab: 20 minutes are the four lessons' own short mini-exercises (5 minutes each, listed per-lesson below), and the remaining 30 minutes are the separate final practical lab (student-lab/). 20 + 30 = 50. This note exists so lesson-level practical minutes and the lab's own estimated duration are never double-counted against each other.

lessons.title: Detecting Missing Values with isna()
lessons.objective: Use isna()/isnull() and column-level summaries to find and count missing values in a pandas DataFrame.

lessons.title: Filling and Dropping Missing Values Deliberately
lessons.objective: Apply fillna() and dropna() with an explicit, column-specific strategy instead of removing all incomplete rows by default.

lessons.title: Detecting Duplicate Rows with duplicated()
lessons.objective: Use duplicated() with default and subset arguments to detect exact-row and business-key duplicates.

lessons.title: Removing Duplicates Deterministically with drop_duplicates()
lessons.objective: Use drop_duplicates() with keep and subset to remove duplicate rows in a reproducible, documented way.
